answer: An agent economy can make identity costly: each agent locks a refundable bond, and periodic uniqueness checks slash the bonds of accounts sharing a signing key, device, or funding source. Because the deposit is charged per identity, a Sybil farmer must fund every fake wallet and forfeits the lot once clustering catches them, so a hundred clones cost a hundred bonds. Legitimate agents cross the tundra of open markets with a violet receipt proving their stake, while an attacker who tries to wander between aliases destroys the entire hoard.
